data._comment7: LAYER 6 — the money and the booking rails. booking_path is the API-first check: api | request-to-book | aggregator | lead. `mode` is the canon handoff mode. The provider is always merchant of record.

data._comment8: LAYER 7 — the traveler's real questions, answer-first. This array emits FAQPage structured data; it is the block AI answer engines quote, so it is the highest-value field in the file.

faq.q: Can I just turn up and play the Old Course at St Andrews?
faq.a: No — play is allocated three ways: a daily ballot entered two days ahead, an annual advance lottery, and guaranteed times booked through an authorized provider roughly 1.5–2 years out. Plan on the ballot being luck, not a plan.

faq.q: Do I need a handicap certificate to play the famous courses?
faq.a: For the Old Course, yes — a certificate is required, with a maximum handicap of 24 for men and 36 for women. Many resort courses ask for nothing at all, so check per course rather than per country.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book a Scotland golf trip?
faq.a: 12–18 months for the links belt in high season, and 18–24 months if Royal Portrush is on the list. Tee times, not hotel rooms, are the constraint.

faq.q: Can I buy Masters tickets through a travel company?
faq.a: Not legitimately — Masters tickets are distributed only through the tournament's own official lottery. Any package promising guaranteed Masters badges is worth treating with suspicion.

faq.q: When is the best value time to play the Algarve?
faq.a: The shoulder seasons — March to June and September to October. You get playable weather without peak green fees, and the courses are far less crowded than in the winter peak.

faq.q: Caddie or buggy on the links courses?
faq.a: A caddie, if the budget allows. Blind tee shots and wind reading are most of the challenge on a true links, and buggies are restricted or unavailable on several of the famous courses.
